title: Peru severs diplomatic ties with Iran
summary:
Peru severs diplomatic ties with Iran

Peru announced that it has decided to end diplomatic relations with Iran, as tensions in the Middle East escalate. 

The country's foreign ministry said the decision was driven by Lima's "historic commitment to peace". 

 The statement added that Peru watched with growing concern "the deterioration of democratic values in Iran," including what it said was Tehran's "repression of peaceful demonstrations, the curtailment of freedom of the press, discrimination against women and girls, and the persecution of political opponents".

It also warned of possible repercussions for energy prices and global supply chains, amid disruptions to international trade through the strategic Strait of Hormuz. 

Peru has rejected Iran's "incitement to violence and the escalation of conflicts in the Middle East, as well as its obstruction of the work of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)".

Although it would be cutting off ties with Tehran, Lima indicated that consular relations would remain in order to protect the interests and nationals of both countries.

title: US energy secretary says 17 million barrels of oil transited Hormuz Strait on Monday
summary:
US energy secretary says 17 million barrels of oil transited Hormuz Strait on Monday

US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said that 17 million barrels of oil transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.

Wright added that marked the highest level of crude oil to pass through the waterway since the war on Iran disrupted shipping.

Wright's statement shows a discrepancy with preliminary ship-tracking data from Kpler, which recorded only five commodity vessels transiting the waterway that day, with no liquid tankers recorded.

The data does not include vessels that have their transponders switched off as it reduces their visibility.

title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
summary:
Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever.

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

title: US missile strikes target areas near Iran's Ahvaz and Aghajari
summary:
US missile strikes target areas near Iran's Ahvaz and Aghajari

Two locations near the cities of Ahvaz and Aghajari in Iran’s south western Khuzestan province were targeted in missile strikes, state media reported citing the province’s deputy governor for security affairs.

title: IRGC says missile strikes destroyed US facilities, killed pilots in Jordan
summary:
IRGC says missile strikes destroyed US facilities, killed pilots in Jordan

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced strikes on US facilities in Jordan in retaliation to Washington's attack on a wedding, which killed and wounded several civilians. 

The IRGC said that it carried out a "heavy attack" using ballistic missiles targeting RQ-4 and MQ-9 drone hangars at Prince Hassan airbase, claiming that it resulted in the destruction of a number of drones as well as killing pilots and flight crew members.

It added that several technical infrastructures were also set on fire.

title: US strike on wedding ceremony in Iran's Sirik kills at least four people
summary:
US strike on wedding ceremony in Iran's Sirik kills at least four people

At least four people, including a child, have been killed in a US attack on Tuesday in a residential area near the Iranian city of Sirik, local media reported, citing the Iranian Red Crescent Society’s provincial branch.

The US strike occurred during a wedding, wounding over 50 people. Rescue efforts in the area remain ongoing.

title: Iran says attacks on US will continue 'until they regret their crime'
summary:
Iran says attacks on US will continue 'until they regret their crime'

The spokesperson of Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned that operations against the US will "continue as a lesson to them until they regret their crime".

Ebrahim Zolfaghari said in a statement carried by the official IRNA news agency that Iran responded to American attacks that have killed civilians.

He added that Tehran's retaliation caused heavy damage to infrastructure, facilities, weapons and equipment, and that a "significant number" of US commanders and soldiers were killed or wounded.

"This offensive operation will continue as a lesson against the Americans until they regret their crime," Zolfaghari said.

"We warn that the continuation of American evil in the region will be met with heavier, broader, and more devastating responses, and any country that cooperates with the aggressive American army must accept its dangerous consequences."
